O R D E R Leave granted.

2. We have heard learned senior counsel for the appellant; learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 3; learned counsel for respondent Nos.4 to 7 who are proforma respondents and learned counsel for the applicant.
3. I.A. No.77809/2020

for intervention/impleadment is allowed since the said impleading applicant states that he is the allottee of the land belonging to appellant herein which has been acquired by the official respondents (respondent Nos.1 to 3) and has been subsequently allotted to the impleading applicant, in respect of which there is also a challenge pending before the High Court filed by the appellant herein.

4. By the impugned order dated 13.12.2013 passed in C.W.P No.7568/2001, the Punjab and Haryana High Court followed the judgment of the Division Bench of the said High Court in Civil Writ Petition No. 7050/2001 titled as Jasmer Singh and Others vs. State of Punjab and Others decided on 19.04.2011 and consequently, dismissed the Writ Petition filed by the appellant herein.
5.

6.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents in unison submitted that firstly, the appellant herein filed the Writ Petition subsequent to the award being passed and that was one of the reasons for dismissal of the Writ Petition by the High Court; secondly, the judgment of this Court in Karnail Kaur was passed by this Court prior to the judgment of the larger Bench of this Court in Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and Others (2020) 8 SCC 129 (Indore Development Authority) on the basis of the law as it stood then which was Pune Municipal Corporation & Anr. vs.
Harakchand Misrimal Solanki & Ors (2014) 3 SCC 183 (Pune Municipal Corporation).

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and Others (2020) 8 SCC 129 (Indore Development Authority)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Pune Municipal Corporation & Anr. vs.
Harakchand Misrimal Solanki & Ors (2014) 3 SCC 183 (Pune Municipal Corporation)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Today, the judgment in Indore Development Authority which is holding the field has to be applied to the present case if the application filed by the appellant under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act has to be considered.

They further submitted that the judgment of this Court in Karnail Kaur following the judgment in Pune Municipal Corporation cannot be a precedent to the instant case and at best that judgment would bind the parties to the said case, as Pune Municipal Corporation is no longer a good law and has been overruled by a larger Bench of this Court in Indore Development Authority.

Thus,
learned counsel for the respondents submitted that there is no merit in this appeal and the same may be dismissed.

7. In response to this submission, learned senior counsel for the appellant submitted that if this Court is inclined to consider the application filed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act, the matter may be remitted to the High Court for consideration of the same on the basis of the records and on the basis of the contentions which would arise in the case.

Learned senior counsel submitted that if this Court is inclined to remit the matter to the High Court for the purpose of consideration of the case on the basis of Indore Development Authority and having regard to the records of the present case, then appropriate orders may be made.
8. We have considered the arguments advanced at the bar.

We note that Karnail Kaur was decided by this Court on the basis of Pune Municipal Corporation, but that judgment no longer holds the field and has in fact been overruled by a larger Bench in Indore Development Authority.

If the application filed by the appellant herein under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act is to be considered today, it would require a consideration and perusal of the records of the case so as to apply the dictum of this Court in Indore Development Authority.
9.

In the circumstances, we set aside the impugned order of the High Court; remand the matter to the High Court for reconsideration of the case, inter alia, on the basis of the dictum of this Court in Indore Development Authority by considering, inter alia, the application filed by the appellant herein under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.
10.
Since we are remanding the matter without considering the case on merits, we have not observed anything on the merits of this case.

Consequently, the parties are at liberty to raise all contentions that are available to them in law in the Writ Petition having regard to the records and having regard to the events that have transpired in this case and having regard to the judicial precedent.
